title: Optimize quantized kernels (INT8/FP8): smoothquant + dequant fusion + KV-cache & continuous batching improvements
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Improve production throughput and tail latency for quantized inference (INT8/FP8) workloads by adding a fused dequantization execution path, integrating smoothquant scaling into the kernel pipeline, and reducing contention in KV-cache hot paths when continuous batching is enabled. This PR targets the runtime kernels and scheduling layer; no public API changes.

Summary of changes: merged a new fused dequant path into the quantized GEMM kernel, added smoothquant pre-scale/out-scale helpers that are applied at op boundary to reduce dynamic range issues in INT8/FP8 conversions, refactored the per-request KV-cache lookup to reduce mutex contention under high-concurrency continuous batching, and improved batcher scheduling heuristics to prioritize low-latency small-batches while maintaining high throughput for large-batch scenarios.

Benchmarks (internal perf harness, p95 latency and token/sec):
- Baseline (vmain) on A10: 1000 tokens/sec, p95 72ms
- This PR on A10: 1600 tokens/sec (+60%), p95 58ms (-19%)
- Baseline on T4: 620 tokens/sec, p95 95ms
- This PR on T4: 980 tokens/sec (+58%), p95 76ms (-20%)
Quantized model correctness: numerical diffs vs fp16 baseline are within expected tolerance after smoothquant scaling and fused dequant rounding.

Files changed (high-level): runtime/kernels/quantized_gemm.cc runtime/kernels/quantized_gemm.h runtime/kernels/smoothquant.h runtime/scheduling/batcher.cc runtime/cache/kv_cache.cc runtime/cache/kv_cache.h tests/perf/bench_quant_kernels.py docs/perf/quant-kernels.md

Implementation notes:
- Kernel-level: added DequantFusePath that fuses int8/uint8 -> fp32 dequant and matmul accumulation with a single memory pass when input layout allows. The path includes a small fast-path for FP8 block formats used by some open models. SmoothQuant scaling factors are applied at input pack and output unpack to keep dynamic range within quantizer limits.
- Scheduling: batcher now tracks per-model sequence-length distribution and dynamically adjusts the continuous-batching window; low-latency tokens are pushed to a prioritized lane that uses a smaller batching window.
- KV-cache: switched to sharded reader-writer locks + per-shard lock-free LRU hinting. This reduced high-contention cases where many concurrent requests with long prefixes would block on a global lock.
- Tests: added microbenchmarks and unit tests validating fused path correctness, plus a perf harness entry showing end-to-end latency/throughput improvements.

Checklist: 
- [x] Kernel fused dequant path implemented
- [x] SmoothQuant integration with unit tests
- [x] KV-cache contention fixes + tests
- [x] Batcher heuristic adjustments + smoke tests
- [x] Perf numbers validated on A10/T4
- [x] Documentation updated with guidance and configuration knobs

How to test locally: run pytest tests/perf/bench_quant_kernels.py::test_a10_end2end --benchmark-save=pr-130999 and compare results to the provided baseline in tests/perf/baselines. For microkernel verification build with KERN_DEBUG=1 and run unit tests in runtime/kernels.

Related work: builds on previous quant-kernel improvements (see ENG-1243, ENG-1310) and addresses regressions observed in canary runs for continuous batching under heavy KV-cache reuse.

Notes: initial CI run had a flaky perf benchmark failure (unit-tests failed due to timing nondeterminism) which was rerun and passed; the PR required one follow-up commit to tighten a float comparison in tests. No breaking changes to API or configs beyond new runtime knobs exposed in docs.
